theses.title: The one-paragraph story
theses.text:
## The one-paragraph story

A predecessor system (not present in this repo) proved the concept and then
collapsed under its own success: roughly 140 accumulated feedback rules loaded
as prose pushed fresh sessions toward 400–500k tokens of always-on context,
where rules fired wrongly or vanished when needed most. In the project's RPG
vocabulary, it brought the **whole stash into every map** — as if a character
carried gear for every damage type when the encounter called only for cold
resistance. In plain language, irrelevant rules consumed attention and created
unintended interactions before the task began. The author's implementation
answers with _compiled_ rules: each correction becomes a typed mechanism (a
permission, a guard, a reactor, an evaluator, a transformer, a workflow gate)
attached only where relevant. A session in that profile gets **a build, not a
biography** — one active behavior, a handful of linked supports, its selected
safety layer, and the exact task state. The platform supplies the compiler and
mechanism contracts without prescribing that loadout. The [starter proof](../evidence/WO-118/README.md) completed resident-owned scratch delivery and review repair with writer replacement and resident restart; a fresh export demonstrated live status, while efficiency remains unmeasured.

theses.title: The core bet
theses.text:
## The core bet

> "The true work of the inventor consists in choosing among these combinations
> so as to eliminate the useless ones... the rules that must guide the choice
> are extremely fine and delicate. It's almost impossible to state them
> precisely; they must be felt rather than formulated." — Poincaré, via Pirsig

Generation is cheap and getting cheaper; the scarce asset is the **selection
function** — the operator's sense of what is good, currently exercised one
correction at a time. DotLn's bet is not that this delicate judgment can be
exhaustively formulated. It is that useful operational approximations can be
progressively arrived at: source incidents preserve what was felt, candidate
mechanisms approach it from different directions, and regression fixtures show
where each construction agrees or diverges. As mathematical or geometric
techniques can converge on a shape without becoming the shape itself, the
formulation is an instrument for approaching the operator's selection function,
not a claim to contain it precisely. **The model changes; the organization
survives.** Claude, Codex, a human, a shell script, and a future model are
interchangeable occupants of the same actor slot.

That bet needs an excellent foundation before it needs a long feature list. In
the reference implementation, the smallest useful loop—declare intent, see what
the system understood, observe authorized progress, receive timely feedback,
and inspect evidence—should already feel responsive, legible, and worth
repeating. Competitive gap-filling does not excuse a weak loop. When another
system introduces a useful idea, DotLn first asks whether the exact behavior can
be accommodated by existing primitives, compositions, ports, and runtime
lowerings. If not, the difference becomes evidence for one missing primitive or
boundary, not permission to bolt on an opaque special case. Integration and
semantic accommodation are preferred to imitation; both preserve every
capability contract the receiving implementation declares and expose any
omitted or lossy capability.

theses.title: The differentiated interface
theses.text:
## The differentiated interface

DotLn's second thesis is about _authoring_, not running:

> "I will take the entire Business, Leadership, and Personal Development shelf
> at Barnes & Noble and just map them to different agent / subagent
> communication structures... at once anyone who has read those books is an
> expert in some feature of the app — and it turns all those books into
> programming books overnight."

The analogies are not documentation — **the analogies are the ways you mix and
match the agents**. Every pattern (5S, the Ladder of Leadership, mitigated
speech, Theory of Constraints, commedia dell'arte roles, the
Algorithms-to-Live-By policies) compiles into exact mechanics, and the same
compiled program renders through an open-ended set of isomorphically equivalent
views: an RPG character with a Path-of-Exile-style socket-and-link build, a
business pattern card, a statechart, a function table, a marble/Morse temporal
track, a TypeScript DSL, an event timeline. Friendly metaphors are authoring
languages, never camouflage: every view either provably compiles to the same
normalized program or is labeled a lossy projection with the exact mechanics one
click away.

### Shape-first synthesis

The operator uses situations and analogies to communicate a desired **shape**: a
relationship, interaction, transition, contrast, feedback loop, or felt quality.
Literal similarity to the reference is not the acceptance test unless a specific
literal detail becomes load-bearing. Preserve the experience first, then
progressively lower it through observable interaction, domain mechanics,
contracts and evidence, and finally technology selected from representative
environment evidence. An imperfect analogy can carry a precise requirement;
source accidents do not become ontology by resemblance.

This is the standing interpretation rule for earlier and future operator
ideation. Its fullest product expression is the first-party application thesis,
[`προτείνω`](11-protino.md), but it applies to the whole platform.

theses.title: Three horizons, one kernel
theses.text:
## Three horizons, one kernel

1. **Work operating system** — workstreams, disposable workers, evidence-backed
   completion, offline-capable state, a near-empty main thread. The immediate
   product.
2. **Executable pattern workshop** — the shelf-to-mechanism compiler and the
   drag-a-card-onto-an-agent authoring surface. The differentiated product.
3. **Agent ecology & simulation laboratory** — paired counterfactual runs,
   first-divergence detection, agent swaps, reflection-policy experiments over
   recorded event logs. The research product.

Horizon 3 must emerge from the same kernel (deterministic replay is what makes
counterfactuals possible at all) and is not allowed to distort Horizon 1.
The [workstream application candidate](12-workstream-application.md) develops
Horizon 1 through concrete end-user journeys and gradual workflow replacement,
including one outcome spanning multiple repositories. It leaves deployment and
application identity open and does not allocate another release rung.
[`προτείνω`](11-protino.md) is the operator-named application destination that
joins Horizons 2 and 3: prose-authored patterns and ad hoc interventions become
playable inside an inspectable counterfactual community. Naming the destination
does not move it ahead of the release ladder or make its application-local
content kernel doctrine.

theses.title: Mission — increase the chance of operator flow
theses.text:
## Mission — increase the chance of operator flow

This is the mission of the author's personal implementation and a motivating
use of the platform, not a compulsory objective or operating policy for every
DotLn owner.

AI-assisted work commonly falls into a babysitting mode: the operator repeatedly
restates context, supplies procedural guidance, coordinates tools and workers,
checks unsupported completion claims, recovers stalled work, and spends active
attention on the machinery instead of the idea. The desired alternative is not
unbounded improvisation or confidence without evidence. It is a sustained
creative flow in which the operator can keep the idea and implementation
direction in mind while the surrounding work behaves dependably.

The reference implementation's mission is to improve the conditions for that
**operator flow state**.
Supporting research, capability-building, coordination, routine procedure,
recovery, and verification should happen automatically when authorized,
predictably when routine, and helpfully when a genuinely material decision needs
the operator. Product and research investment should favor capabilities that
remove recurring supervision and avoidable context switches without exporting
their cost into correctness, authority, evidence, privacy, or recoverability.

The implementation cannot promise or infer a person's psychological state. It can
reduce interruption, repetition, manual ceremony, and rediscovery; preserve
intent and working context across handoffs; package necessary interruptions as
decision-ready inputs; and make recovery unsurprising. Under its selected
profile, flow does not silently authorize scope expansion, skipped verification,
perpetual action, or self-certification. “Give an agent a build, not your
biography” remains useful architectural shorthand for one mechanism serving
this larger mission.

exclusions.text:
Not an agent, an agent harness, or an agent-orchestration layer, as its
  identity. DotLn is an **agentic platform**: the shared substrate on which
  people and software actors hold work, authority, and evidence. It contains an
  orchestration layer and hosts harnesses as observed environments
  ([runtime primitive catalogs](03-architecture.md#runtime-primitive-catalogs)),
  but neither of those is what it is.
Not a prompt library, and not a wrapper that makes one vendor's model nicer.

Not a prescribed catalog of ideal agents, roles, personalities, workflows, or
  organizational doctrine. Bundled patterns are examples and optional starting
  points, not kernel truth.

Not dependent on a public marketplace. Local files, private catalogs,
  organization-internal registries, and offline or air-gapped installations
  remain complete authoring and distribution paths.

Not one prescribed autonomy curve. Presence and recorded time are policy
  inputs; an explicit owner policy may hold, shrink, grow, peak, reset, or loop
  scope and authority within its declared ceiling.

In the reference implementation, not a metrics theater: no invented numbers,
  no activity-as-progress, evidence precedes "done," and utilization is not the
  objective. A profile that omits verification says so instead.

The reference implementation is not finished when it works for its author:
  v1.0 means a person who has never read these docs can declare a bounded intent
  and receive a verifiable result.

orders.objective:
Every core release reaches DotLn-Enterprise-Starter with no
hand-run step. After `release close WO-NNN --publish` has published (or
re-confirmed) the tag and its Release, the helper, in a launchpad whose
sibling declaration names an export sibling with a recorded local checkout,
runs the export update for the released commit into a disposable worktree
of that checkout (or, while the starter holds no `KIT-MANIFEST.json`, the
first export of that commit), verifies the result the way an export verifies itself,
commits it once and pushes that commit as a fast-forward of the starter's
`main` to the starter's own repository, fast-forwards the checkout, writes
WO-078's receipt into main's ignored lane for the next `worktree start` to
carry into a reviewed change, and records the run in the close record and
summary. A missing, dirty, diverged or misbound checkout, a refused plan
row or a failed verification refuses before any push, leaves the checkout
and the remote as they were, and is recorded as a close blocker with the
same retry command. Nothing is pushed anywhere else: not core's main, not
a tag, not another branch, and never the operator's fork.

criteria.text:
`release close WO-NNN --publish`, after the tag and Release exist (the
   published path and the equal-version retry), in a launchpad whose
   declaration names an export sibling with a recorded checkout, pushes
   to that sibling's repository exactly one commit whose parent is the
   remote `main` head, as a fast-forward of `refs/heads/main`, with no
   other ref and no tag changed and no force; the commit's
   `KIT-MANIFEST.json` names the released commit and tag; the checkout ends
   clean at the pushed commit and no disposable worktree remains; main's
   tracked and untracked non-ignored state is unchanged (step 6, case a).
   While the starter's `origin/main` holds no `KIT-MANIFEST.json`, the same
   close performs the first export instead: one commit on top of the
   remote's head holding the export's tree (initial-commit paths the export
   writes take its bytes, others are kept, both listed), pushed as a
   fast-forward of `main`, verified as criterion 2 requires, recorded
   `refreshed` with `firstExport: true`; a file/directory collision with
   the initial commit refuses with nothing pushed; every later release
   takes the update path (step 6, case j).

The refreshed tree passes the export's own emit with every predicted
   surface equal (the operating contract by its marked block), its own
   `harness check` and its own `launchpad verify`, and its staged change set
   is exactly the plan's changed rows, `KIT-MANIFEST.json` and `CLAUDE.md`.
   A refused plan row, a failed emit, check or verify, or any other staged
   path refuses with nothing pushed, the checkout clean at its prior commit,
   no worktree and no receipt (step 6, case g).

Each of these refuses before any write in the checkout or the remote,
   naming the reason: no recorded checkout; a recorded path that is not a
   physical Git top level or is main itself; a checkout not on `main`;
   tracked or untracked non-ignored changes; a local `main` ahead of or
   diverged from `origin/main` after the fetch; an origin push URL, read
   before any rewrite, that does not name core's origin host and owner and
   the sibling's id; no `main` on the remote; a starter
   manifest naming a core commit that is neither an ancestor nor a
   descendant of the released commit. A checkout behind its remote is
   fast-forwarded first. These refusals hold on the first-export path too.
   Main's HEAD past the published tag, or a starter manifest naming a
   descendant of the released commit, makes the row `skipped` with no
   blocker (step 6, cases c to f, i and k).

A rerun after a refresh reports `current` and pushes nothing; a
   `current` row writes a pending receipt only when no committed or pending
   receipt records the starter's manifest hash (step 6, case b; step 8,
   case d).

Every row is recorded in `release-close.json` (`starterRefresh`) and the
   summary prints one line per row; neither names the checkout's path. A
   refused row adds a `starter-refresh` blocker with the same retry
   command, exits nonzero and keeps the dispatch's writer; the publication
   outcome, tag and Release are unchanged by any refresh outcome (step 8,
   cases b to d).

No refresh is attempted for a launchpad with no export sibling declared
   (an exported instance, the operator's fork), a target order, a
   lower-version close, a close without `--publish`, or a dry run, which
   prints the preview and writes nothing; the refresh fetches and pushes
   only the bound starter URL (step 6, case h; step 8, cases a, e, f and g).

After a successful push the receipt, in WO-078's five fields and file
   name, is written only to main's ignored pending lane. The next `worktree
   start` copies each pending receipt into the new worktree's evidence
   root, regenerates the registry there (its `index --check` passes), leaves
   main clean and empties the lane; a malformed pending receipt refuses the
   start with no worktree and no branch (steps 2 and 9).

`worktree clone <id> <absolute-path>` records a declared export
   sibling's checkout in the ignored clone map; a consumer sibling and an
   undeclared id refuse as before (step 3).

Every fixture reaches only local bare remotes behind GitHub URLs
   rewritten in fixture-global Git configuration; no test fetches from or
   pushes to a network remote; the `launchpad` suite gains at most three
   kit preparations (the first export, one update, one failed
   verification); the evidence records the cases' wall-clock and the
   `launchpad` task's duration before and after, with the judgment of
   FUP-b531e850b70f6d4e's condition (steps 6, 8 and 12). No duration binds
   this criterion.

Both forms of the release-close role text name the refresh as the
    helper's one further external effect, forbid every other push, force
    and merge, and make a refusal a reported blocker that never cleans,
    resets or commits in the starter checkout; the bundle is regenerated
    and `npm run harness -- check` passes (step 10).

Write-backs land in place with no dated paragraph: product 07 (the
    release-close row and §Workflow closeout and releases, including the
    authority sentence), product 03, product 12, `docs/PLAYBOOK.md`,
    `docs/AI-HARNESS-SECURITY.md`, `docs/README.md` and the decisions file;
    publication locks refreshed if a locked section changed; product 07
    within its ceiling.

`npm test -- --review` and `npm run test:docs` green; the deterministic
    re-mints of the editions `contributor.ts` stales (authority, feedback
    and harness, as their checks report) recorded; no live feedback episode
    is owed; `git diff --check` clean; no new dependency.

candidate's objects and only then creates the episode branch and updates
refs; the retained counterexample fails against the writer's access;
candidates still publish; a crash between import and ref update recovers

an unjustified success. A writer that reports `status` other than

and the vertical records `NeedsHuman` with the request in its receipt. The

the host imports and observes the commit. `dotln vertical` with a writer killed before commit exits 1
with a pending continuation, and a rerun completes the step with exactly one
commit. Ordinary recovery stays valid throughout.

orders.title: WO-207 — Instance update control: an instance takes kit machinery with its build pinned or followed, keeps its own code at a manifest-excluded extension root that the kit's machinery loads through the SourceAdapter port and no update touches, rolls back its last update to the prior kit state, and takes a starter update only through an upgrade order its own planning pass cuts, gated by kit conformance and its own declared suites (version assigned at activation)
orders.objective:
An instance controls the kit updates it takes, from core and
inside the instance:

- **Its own code.** `dotln.config.json` may declare `extensions`: a root
  outside every kit tree (default `extensions/`) and adapters by kind
  (`source`, `effect`, `projection`). A vertical issue naming
  `source: "<id>"` has `prepare()` load that adapter, record
  `ExtensionLoaded { id, kind, path, sha256 }` and call its `fetchBundle`
  in place of `fetchIssueBundle`, with the bundle passing the same checks
  as the GitHub source's; `effect` and `projection` adapters are admitted
  and listed, never imported here. No export, manifest or update touches
  the root; the README states the review burden. The first consumer is a
  fixture adapter; the enterprise-tracker adapter is the work instance's.
- **Its build.** The kit manifest names its build (the compiled definition
  modules, their semantic hash and compiler version). An update takes
  `both` (today's), `machinery` (build modules kept at their pinned bytes,
  `build.pin` recorded, emit, check and `kit-verify` honoring it) or `build`
  (the build alone, then the re-emit), and refuses an incompatible pairing
  before any write; inside an instance, the upgrade order runs
  `build --pin` or `build --take` after its merge, as the channel the
  operator chose. WO-076's overlay composes over whichever build is pinned.
- **Its way back.** Each update logs what it did and keeps retained copies,
  refusing before any write when it cannot. `rollback` inside the instance,
  or `export --update <dir> --rollback` from core, returns the kit files
  and manifest to the logged state before the last update, reverses the
  reversible instance actions (the update's `build.pin` among them), lists
  the rest by id, logs itself and prints the re-emit, which the role that
  ran it runs next; it refuses, naming the path or row, after a later kit
  edit, when the update is not the latest, or when a prior file has no
  verified source.
- **Its way in.** An instance takes a starter update only through an
  upgrade order that a planning pass (dedicated, or part of one) cuts from
  the kit's template. A planning branch writes only `docs/` and root
  Markdown (WO-135), so the pass never applies kit files. The order
  previews the update (WO-203), merges the named starter revision, runs the
  channel's `build` form, re-emits the build and passes the kit
  conformance tier; the template's rollback form takes the way back the
  same way.
- **Its gate (the planner's proposal, assumption 8).** Kit conformance:
  `kit-verify` on every gate, and the carried kit suites once per kit
  identity, a hash over the manifest-listed paths (and, while the overlay
  question stays open, the overlay file). The instance's own
  additions: suites it declares in `dotln.config.json` `suites` (name,
  command and sources), selected by changed sources, with each extension
  adapter naming the suite that covers it. Core's own gate is unchanged.
- **No step is the operator's by hand.** The operator gives the word (the
  starter revision, the channel, how each refused path resolves, a
  rollback), types the dispatch phrases and merges the pull request; a
  role runs every command and makes every commit (operator direction,
  2026-10-13; planning document §12.1).

   source refuses naming the key, and an absent section loads as none; a

   naming the key, and an absent channel reads as `both` (configuration

   `requireCompleteIssueBundle`, the screen and `decodeSourceBundle` as the
   GitHub source's does, and the record the decisions name holds

Declared `effect` and `projection` adapters are listed by kind with

   runs them (extension cases).

An export from a core checkout carries no path under the extension root

The kit manifest (schema 2) names its build files, semantic hash and

Under `machinery` an update replaces every kit file but the build

   the emitted bundle at the pinned build after the re-emit; under `build`

   write (fixture).

A `machinery` update whose incoming compiler is incompatible with the

goalReview.goalStandard:
## Goal-aligned decisions

The Contributor's purpose comes from [the vision](00-vision.md): DotLn is a
local-first, model-agnostic compiler/runtime for human judgment. This personal
implementation aims to improve operator flow by moving recurring supervision,
coordination, recovery and verification into dependable machinery, while
preserving correctness, authority, evidence, privacy and recoverability.

The current [critical-path plan](../planning/critical-path-2026-09-08.md) targets
the always-on runtime, its first real external source change and an independently
verified source-to-deliverable loop.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:start -->

The [sequence](../planning/sequence.md) and selected work order determine
current placement and authority. The mission is the outcome; the critical path
is the dependency route to the next outcome. Useful prerequisite or
risk-reduction work must name the blocked outcome it enables. Process activity,
receipt volume and agent utilization are not progress by themselves. Goal
alignment grants no authority to reorder or expand work. In all phases, the Goal
Alignment and Process Cost procedure lives in the generated role skills
[WO-043, 2026-09-11].

Accuracy takes priority over agreement in every phase. The already-equipped
Correctness over Sycophancy rule applies to operator suggestions and the agent's
own premises equally: challenge unsupported claims, distinguish observation
from inference, state material uncertainty, and correct mistakes when evidence
changes. A confident request or an earlier decision is not proof of correctness.
Record material disagreement and its evidence in the same decision or phase
receipt; do not manufacture dissent or seek approval for ordinary judgment.

| Lens                                  | Decision question                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Policy resistance / fixes that fail   | Will local goals or guards undo one another?                                                              |
| Tragedy of the commons                | Does the solution consume shared compute, context or operator attention without accounting for the total? |
| Drift to low performance              | Does it improve an explicit outcome standard rather than normalize a worse baseline?                      |
| Escalation                            | Will additional process provoke more process or workarounds?                                              |
| Success to the successful             | Are credible alternatives excluded merely because the current mechanism already has investment?           |
| Shifting the burden to the intervenor | Does the solution remove recurring operator rescue or depend on it?                                       |
| Rule beating                          | Can the evidence pass without the intended behavior occurring?                                            |
| Seeking the wrong goal                | Does it advance operator flow and the selected product outcome rather than a proxy?                       |

Naive Interventionism adds the existing system's useful functions, affected
consumers, second-order harm, reversibility and smallest useful probe. NoOp
records what happens if nothing changes, why action or inaction wins, and the
evidence that would reopen the choice. Scale detail to consequence: explain
applicable risks and briefly group immaterial lenses with a reason; do not
manufacture eight repetitive paragraphs for routine edits.

Record evidence of benefit and the risks of intervening in existing behavior;
verification and handoff compare observed outcomes with the promised benefit.
Required legal or release actions retain their existing authority; NoOp is a
considered alternative, not an ambient veto or permission to abandon authorized
work.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:end -->

**Platform lens.** Four checks from the platforms lesson the operator
pointed at (Steve Yegge's 2011 account of the Amazon service mandate) apply
to any capability a plan or order lands: it arrives as an interface
something else consumes (a transport profile, a typed event, a projection, a
handoff packet), never only as a script or a session; it is externalizable
by construction (content-addressed inputs, declared contracts, no private
setting as the source of a guarantee); this repository and the operator's
own repository consume it before any export; and its result is usable by a
stranger to the session, so a receipt that needs reverse-engineering is an
accessibility failure [[vision-into-use pass](../planning/vision-into-use-2026-09-17.md)
§12, 2026-09-17]. The planning refuter's platform-first standard is
unchanged.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:start -->

Material choices and rationales go in existing phase evidence: per-order
`docs/evidence/WO-NNN/decisions.md` and cited product sections for work-order
decisions; planning dispositions/candidate records for planning choices; the
independent report or refutation receipt for its judgment; retained closeout
evidence for release decisions. The decisions index exposes per-order records.
Reuse and link a current rationale until its assumptions change; do not create
a parallel decision log or an extra approval ritual.

<!-- dotln-goal-rules:end -->

The shared supports carry these duties and their compiled identity in both
harnesses. They are instruction-level judgment, not proof that an agent applied
every lens or a causal detector. The meter's five quantitative trap signals are
separate. General Naive Interventionism, NoOp and adaptive Tinkerer mechanics
retain their candidate scope; this bounded Contributor policy does not claim
their generalized implementations. The [WO-043 receipt](../evidence/WO-043/ideation-commands-and-usage.md)
records this promotion and its limits.

episode.statement: I read <tmp>/refute/prompt.txt in full: the work order, the output and worker instructions, the closed plan-goal-review-v1 schema, and the compiled subject. That subject held the five vision theses, the seven what-dotln-is-not exclusions, the five-role table, the capability rows, the goal standard, the 2026-09-08 critical-path table, the five cost-table trap observations, and the cost table's rows, acceptances and first verifications. It also held the 14-order sequence and each order's title, objective, cost, criteria and non-goals. To read the prompt, I parsed it with a local Python script into scratch files outside the repository, and I checked the result against the schema with a second local script. I judged from that subject alone. I did not read any repository file, planner narrative, earlier receipt or the other file beside the prompt, and I ran no Git command, gate or test. The project and user instruction files present in my session context were not used as evidence. No model or effort claim is made from host readback.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Gate: not named in the subject's critical-path table (2026-09-08). Inference from the subject: it unblocks a precondition of gate P. WO-083's objective presumes a personal instance forked from the starter, while WO-215's title says the starter holds no export yet ('the first export, while the starter holds none') and its own release close performs that first export. It also completes gate S's 'updates carry the rest' for every later release. It is not in WO-083's activation preflight list. NoOp in the records: the cost-table row's metrics are null, so no NoOp cost is measured. The order's own record names what persists without it: a hand-run `launchpad export --update` after each core release, a separate starter commit and push, and the receipt commit WO-078's assumption 2 left to the operator's change (FUP-efcc590126413a41). The starter also stays without any export, so no fork can be taken from it. The hand step recurs at the release rate; its wall-clock is unrecorded.
orders.systemTraps: Rule beating (meter flat; readAmplification 0.95 at WO-118): the refresh is verified the way an export verifies itself (emit with every predicted surface equal, `harness check`, `launchpad verify`), the staged set must equal the plan's rows, and criterion 1 binds the remote ref, so the evidence cannot pass unless the push happened. Seeking the wrong goal (the one reopen candidate: elapsedPerCodeByte worsening 168 -> 198 -> 288 -> 372 across WO-201, WO-202, WO-203 and WO-118): the order adds up to three kit preparations to the `launchpad` gate task, paid on every later core gate run, in exchange for removing a per-release operator step. Criterion 9 records durations but binds none. Shifting the burden (flat): it removes a recurring hand step, but a refused refresh hands the operator a blocker with a retry command (finding). Drift to low performance (coldStart flat; release-close 16,532 bytes against a 21,266 ceiling): about two sentences of role text fit the headroom. Policy resistance (guardRefusals flat at 1): a refusal keeps the dispatch's writer, which the next order's start then meets. Tragedy of the commons: each publishing close spends one kit preparation, update, emit, check, kit verify, commit, fetch and push of shared machine time, all unmeasured. Escalation: one effect under an existing phrase and no new operator command, but a new pending-receipt lane that `worktree start` must carry. Success to the successful: reuses `planKitUpdate`, `applyKitUpdate` and `exportKit` rather than a parallel path; the subject records no alternative route weighed.
orders.removalBalance: Partly. Removed: a recurring per-release operator step (the hand-run export update, its separate commit and push, and the receipt commit), which is operator attention at every release. Added: a new module, one more release-close effect, a pending-receipt lane carried at `worktree start`, an export-sibling admission in `worktree clone`, fixtures across five suites, two role-text sentences, and recurring machine cost: one kit preparation, update, emit, check, kit verify, commit, fetch and push per publishing close, plus up to three kit preparations per `launchpad` gate run. In operator steps the removal is larger. In machine time the balance is unknown until step 12 and the first live close are measured. The cost line does not claim a time saving.
orders.failureBehavior: Mixed. The refresh refuses before any write or push on every listed condition and leaves the checkout and the remote as they were. Tag, Release and publication outcome stay unchanged, and the hand route (`launchpad export --update`) is kept, so the starter can still be refreshed the old way. Absent declarations degrade to today's behaviour: no export sibling, a target order, a lower-version close, no `--publish` or a dry run. But a refused row makes release close exit nonzero, adds a `starter-refresh` blocker and keeps the dispatch's writer (criterion 5). A starter-side cause unrelated to the released order therefore does not degrade to today's outcome (the close completes without a refresh); the close refuses until a retry succeeds.

findings.reason: A refresh refusal holds release close open (nonzero exit, a `starter-refresh` blocker, the dispatch's writer kept) for causes outside the released order: a dirty, diverged or misbound starter checkout, or a missing remote `main`. Publication has already succeeded and the old hand route remains. A persistent starter-side cause therefore blocks the close of a core order whose product work is done, and the next order's activation meets a held writer. The order states that refresh outcomes never change publication. Its failure mode refuses instead of degrading to a recorded follow-up, which would be the old state: the close completes and the row reads refused, with the retry command.
findings.reopenWhen: A release close records a `starter-refresh` blocker with a starter-side cause, and the writer is still held when the next order is due to activate.

findings.reason: Until the next `worktree start`, a successful refresh's WO-078 receipt exists only in main's ignored pending lane. That start then copies it into whatever order begins next, so the receipt rides in an unrelated order's reviewed change and that order's verifier judges a file it did not produce. The lane is emptied at start. If that order is withdrawn or its worktree is discarded unmerged, the receipt is gone, and criterion 4 writes a new pending receipt only on a later `current` rerun of release close.
findings.reopenWhen: No committed or pending receipt records the starter's manifest hash after the order that carried it was withdrawn or its worktree removed unmerged.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Gate: P. WO-083's activation preflight requires WO-210 closed, and WO-083's nonGoals name its target gate, records action and publications as WO-210's subject. WO-192's criterion 9 and WO-213's criterion 6 also consume it. NoOp in the records: cost-table metrics null. The order's record states the NoOp: an exported instance's own order fails at `worktree publish`'s surface step, at `release prepare` from the seeds and at the manifest build. A target order closes only by a hand merge (WO-072's fixture). Records publications demand release notes and a launchpad `npm test` row (41.7 s fresh in the fixture export) instead of the target's own tests, which no lifecycle step runs. The clone's base is updated only by a hand Git step, and store identifiers reach target PR bodies (WO-118-D010). Without it WO-083 cannot activate.
orders.systemTraps: Rule beating (flat): the design resists it. Target claims stand only on target-gate rows bound to the target tree hash and HEAD; stale, failed or missing rows refuse; the records commit is checked by parent, paths and per-record SHA-256. The records publication may skip `npm test` only on a proved unchanged `gateCodeIdentity`. Seeking the wrong goal (worsening): the order grows core's own suites for instance-only behaviour, a recurring cost on every later core gate that is recorded but not bounded (finding). `launchpad-planning` gains a release drive of about twenty lifecycle commands, four surface checks each running six `npm publish --dry-run` rules, and two refute prompts; `target-worktree` and ten other suites grow too. Against it, the merge removes two order cycles (2.29 full runs and 61 minutes of full gate per closed order, per the planning document's figures). Shifting the burden (flat): it removes the hand merge and the hand base update; the operator still types phrases, merges PRs and gives the grant. Drift (flat): about 130 bytes of goal-rule markers enter every role's directed read of product 07; briefings grow by about two sentences; role text is WO-192's, so no cold-start ceiling moves here. Policy resistance (flat): between WO-210's close and WO-192's, role text names launchpad `npm test` while WO-210's completions refuse it for target orders (finding). Tragedy of the commons: a target gate spends whatever the target's declared commands take; DotLn-Angular's is unknown. Escalation: roles get four new command forms and there is one new control event (`TargetRecordsCommitted`), each a target-order analogue of an existing primitive rather than a new concept; with 24 criteria, and first verification failed for 5 of the last 8 orders, repair cycles are the likely cost driver. Success to the successful: reuses the episode route's lint and body profile; core paths and historical hashes are unchanged.
orders.removalBalance: Yes for the one-time cost, unknown for the recurring residue. Removed: four blocking failures of instance orders, a hand merge, a hand base update, release notes on a branch that releases nothing, the instance's duplicate copies of target records, store identifiers in target bodies, and two order cycles from the merge. Also removed is a launchpad `npm test` row for each target-order claim and records publication (41.7 s in the fixture export). Added: one large change set (24 criteria) and recurring gate time in about a dozen core suites; the executor measures it against the base, but nothing bounds it. A target order's own gate time is unknown. The named removals exceed the one-time addition; whether they exceed the recurring core-gate addition is unknown until measured.
orders.failureBehavior: Degrades for core and for an instance's self orders. Core surfaces, goal standard, historical subject hashes and self-order gate claims are unchanged (criteria 4, 6, 17, 19). In a kit, an undeclared `docs/LEGAL.md` and an undeclared purpose are reported as unavailable instead of failing (criteria 2, 6). Target-order paths refuse by design: missing, failed or stale target-gate rows; a dirty target; a mismatched records commit; a profile or operator grant that does not admit both effects; a lint or local-terms failure. Each refusal comes before any remote call and leaves segments byte-identical (criteria 10, 11, 18, 21). Today those paths have no working automated route (only a hand merge), so there is no automated behaviour to fall back to; the hand route stays possible.

findings.reason: After `resume target-records`, the order's decisions and its verification and final-review reports leave the instance. They live only in a records-only commit in the target, and the instance keeps the repository, commit, path and SHA-256 of each. Containment after squash or rebase merges is a nonGoal. If the target squash- or rebase-merges the pull request, the recorded commit becomes unreachable from the target's base, and the instance's evidence depends on the forge keeping an unmerged commit. The hashes preserve integrity, not availability; the mission asks that machinery not export its cost into evidence or recoverability.
findings.reopenWhen: A registered target's pull request is squash- or rebase-merged and a `TargetRecordsCommitted` commit is not reachable from the target's base branch, or a linked record cannot be fetched by its recorded commit and path.

findings.reason: WO-210 makes a target order's completions refuse launchpad `npm test` rows, while the role text keeps naming launchpad `npm test` until WO-192 rewrites it. WO-210's nonGoals say 'WO-192 writes the role text', and WO-192's cost speaks of 'the launchpad `npm test` the role text still names'. The briefings carry the target gate. For any target order run between the two closes, including the foundational Angular work WO-083 presumes the instance has done, the role text and the refusal disagree: two local guards pull in opposite directions.
findings.reopenWhen: A target order executed between WO-210's and WO-192's closes records a refused completion citing a launchpad `npm test` row, or a repair caused by following the role text over the briefing.

findings.reason: The one worsening trap indicator is elapsed time per code byte (168 -> 198 -> 288 -> 372 over WO-201, WO-202, WO-203 and WO-118; machinery share 0.35 at WO-118). WO-210 puts instance-only scenarios into core suites that every later core order pays: a release drive and a target-order drive in `launchpad-planning`, plus growth in `target-worktree` and ten other suites. These are recorded against the base with no bound. The merge saving is one-time; the suite growth recurs.
findings.reopenWhen: WO-210's recorded suite durations show `launchpad-planning` or `target-worktree` growing by a material share of the full gate, or the cost table's elapsedPerCodeByte worsens again at the next counted order.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Gate: P. WO-083's activation preflight requires WO-213 closed, and it screens the records WO-210 writes into a registered target. NoOp in the records: cost-table metrics null. The order's record: the screen reaches Markdown only (WO-188 D014's first limit); 291 record lines in 37 files hold a home path at 6dbd8771; the follow-up register stores one; and a record carried by WO-210 could put a home path into DotLn-Angular, which is public (product 12).
orders.systemTraps: Rule beating (flat): a new or edited line fails at its file and line, and the message never prints the path. Existing lines are grandfathered by a baseline of fingerprints, not by a waiver flag, and the retained script reproduces the addition (criterion 2), so the baseline cannot be widened silently. Seeking the wrong goal (worsening): docs-check reads 3,544 files and 206.9 MB on every run (255-922 ms in the drafting worker's rounds), a small recurring cost that criterion 7 measures before and after. Shifting the burden (flat): screens refuse before writing, so the operator is not the last line of defence; no operator step is added. Drift (flat): cold-start text grows only by two write-back sentences; the baseline grows about 24 KB (estimate) and is not read at cold start. Policy resistance (flat): seven write paths refuse one more input class. The Entropy Reducer's filing, the runner's task record and the lifecycle control logs stay outside the screen (nonGoals), so they cannot undo it, but they also stay unscreened. Tragedy of the commons: a whole-file test before line splitting keeps the read bounded. Escalation: no new command and no baseline-writing command. Success to the successful: moves the existing pattern into one shared module instead of adding a second scanner.
orders.removalBalance: Yes. Removed: the Markdown-only reach, the register's stored home path, the hand-baseline route, and the risk of a home path reaching a public target repository. Added: one module, a per-type rule, about 24 KB of baseline (estimate), fixtures in five suites, and a recurring sub-second docs-check read. The privacy risk removed outweighs the added cost.
orders.failureBehavior: Degrades. Any pattern the rule misses (`/var/tmp`, `/root`, escaped forms: D014's other limits) passes as it does today; other file types are not read; existing records are untouched. The refusals are the intended effect at write time, for receipts and plan-refutation events, the register sync, target records and the target-scoped planning publication. Each leaves the repositories, branches, remote refs and control segment byte-identical (criteria 5, 6).

findings.reason: The fingerprint baseline accepts 291 committed home-path lines in 37 files, and the nonGoals keep the bytes in earlier commits and any pushed remote. The order stops new exposure but records the existing exposure as accepted without any decision on removing it, and no other order in the horizon addresses it. The mission lists privacy among the costs machinery must not export.
findings.reopenWhen: An operator or planning decision requires removing the existing home paths, or a baselined line is found in a record that a target repository or the starter receives.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Gate: P, first link in the table's chain ('WO-080 -> WO-081, WO-082 -> WO-083'); its prerequisite WO-071 has shipped. WO-083's criterion 3 requires `WS-001` in the shape WO-080 defines, and WO-080's cost says 'WO-083 depends on this order'. NoOp in the records: cost-table metrics null. The order's record: 'workstream' is vocabulary only, and no workstream document, field, grouping, board section or demonstration fixture exists. The configured `workstreams` root is used only by the export's seed, whose text says the index does not read the field. Without it WO-083 cannot meet its criterion 3.
orders.systemTraps: Rule beating (flat): the demonstrations are named fixtures with their own assertions over real Git. `index --check` regenerates the grouping from the committed line alone, so the check cannot pass on host state. Out-of-set cases are follow-ups, which is an explicit limit, not a loophole. Seeking the wrong goal (worsening): the order adds a permanent real-Git `workstream-pilot` suite (three target repositories and an exported launchpad) to every later fresh gate, plus one timed `npm test -- --fresh` measurement. Its wall-clock is unknown, and it removes nothing that runs today (finding). Shifting the burden (flat): no operator step is added; D3, D5 and the conflict half of D4 stay register candidates. Drift (flat): no role text; product 04 was near its ceiling at 5f3849ec and is re-measured at the base. Policy resistance (flat): the writer unit's refusal is exercised, not bypassed. Tragedy of the commons: the suite's machine time is shared by every later order. Escalation: no events or schema changes, and the board section is additive. Success to the successful: reuses WO-071's Repository field, WO-072's target worktrees and the board's view model.
orders.removalBalance: No, measured against NoOp. The cost line says it 'removes nothing that runs today'; its only removal is the merge (two order cycles against running three orders, each cycle 2.29 full runs and 61 minutes of full gate). Against doing nothing it is a pure addition, justified as WO-083's prerequisite and as the first grouping of orders into outcomes. The recurring addition, the new suite in every later fresh gate, is unmeasured.
orders.failureBehavior: Degrades. An unreadable target shows `unknown`; a moved base shows stale; `index --check` regenerates from the committed line without the targets; a view without the Workstreams section still renders and validates against the unchanged schema; an order without a `**Workstream:**` field indexes as today. No event or schema changes.

findings.reason: The worsening trap indicator is elapsed time per code byte (168 -> 198 -> 288 -> 372 over the last four counted orders). WO-080 adds a real-Git suite with three target repositories and an exported launchpad to every later fresh gate. It removes nothing that runs today and records the suite's wall-clock without bounding it. This is the recurring machinery cost that indicator measures; the order's justification is gate P alone.
findings.reopenWhen: The executor's timed fresh run shows the `workstream-pilot` row as a material share of the fresh gate, or the fresh `npm test` exceeds the six-minute stand-down reversal condition with the new suite included.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Gate: P. WO-083's activation preflight requires the three WO-112 source-writer boundaries (cleanup revocation, writer-resistant Git interpretation, shared-object protection) closed by WO-204, and names WO-204 as carrying the resident intent route's source-writer items. It also hardens the source-change primitive of gates D and E and the loop of gate V. NoOp in the records: cost-table metrics null. The record lists what stays open without it. D043: an unlink error bypasses the `WorkerInterrupted` and integrity records, and a revocation flag can claim an effect that did not happen. D044: a clean porcelain status is taken as proof of committed bytes, and verification reads Git configuration, replace refs and a commit graph the writer can steer. D033: a writer can write existing shared objects that nothing inventories. From WO-118-D019: F2 (admission never reads `status` or `requiresHuman`), F3 (rr-cache write, detached maintenance and exit 128 under the Codex grants) and F5 (an untested killed-writer path). FUP-42ef16541a8893b9: the Claude writer's rr-cache and maintenance writes in the shared repository. Without it, the writer can damage the operator's repository during WO-083's run.
orders.systemTraps: Rule beating (flat): the design resists it. The D033 counterexample fails at the base and must pass at the subject; criterion 5 asserts no admission while any grant survives, over every case of the matrix; and the live probes require host-observed facts (a commit in the private store, no rr-cache) rather than the writer's report. Seeking the wrong goal (worsening): the skeleton suite (289.9 s thirty-day median) and the vertical suite (725.851 s at WO-199's repair gate) grow, recorded at handoff. Each episode adds one `cat-file` per tracked path and one fetch. These costs buy safety, not a proxy measure. Shifting the burden (flat): writer requests now reach the operator as `NeedsHuman`, a material interruption, but with no answer route (finding). Drift (flat): no role text; product 03 changes in place. Policy resistance (flat): fail-closed refusals may add guard refusals, recorded as typed outcomes. Tragedy of the commons: at most two live Codex and two live Claude episodes (each Claude episode capped at USD 3.00) and one live feedback episode. Escalation: four orders become one 25-criterion order with three re-mint families. First verification failed for 5 of the last 8 orders, so repair cycles are the likely cost driver. Success to the successful: a host-owned commit or a files-only writer is named as the reopening alternative, not excluded.
orders.removalBalance: Yes. Removed: three boundary classes, F2, F3, F5, FUP-42ef16541a8893b9, three order cycles (each 2.29 full review-gate runs and 61 minutes of full gate per closed order; verification median 16.9 minutes, final review 24.8) and three of the four feedback re-mints and live feedback self-host episodes the four orders owed. Added: containment code, fixtures, suite time, per-episode Git reads and bounded live probes. The safety removal plus the three saved cycles exceed the addition.
orders.failureBehavior: Refuses by design, which is right for containment. A surviving grant, a flagged or differing tracked file, an imported tree that differs, or a writer request each ends in a typed refusal or hold before admission, with nothing restored. The old behaviour (admit) is the defect being removed. Ordinary recovery of an unreceipted prior attempt stays valid (criterion 9), candidates still publish (criterion 12), and a crash before or after import recovers idempotently (criterion 13). A writer request is terminal for its step: a rerun returns the same outcome with no new dispatch.

findings.reason: A writer's request ends its step as `writer-requested-attention`, and the vertical records `NeedsHuman` with the request. But resuming a held step on the operator's answer is a nonGoal, and a rerun returns the same refusal without a dispatch. The request therefore reaches the operator with no route back into the episode: each answer costs a new intent or hand handling. The mission asks for necessary interruptions to be packaged as decision-ready inputs with unsurprising recovery.
findings.reopenWhen: A live `NeedsHuman` hold is answered by the operator, and continuing requires a new intent, a hand step or a planning pass.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Gate: P, as one of WO-083's two admissible routes. WO-083's criterion 1 accepts WO-192's criterion 9 (a phase worker completing its phrase in a target worktree) or a recorded `resume: next` in an operator-opened target-worktree session, so WO-192 is not strictly blocking. NoOp in the records: cost-table metrics null. The order's record: the operator types one phrase per phase into a separate terminal and carries each handoff by hand. That is at least four sessions for an order that passes first time, and more per repair; first verification failed for 5 of the last 8 orders. For target orders the operator opens sessions inside target repositories, and executors repeat full gate runs without a relevant change.
orders.systemTraps: Rule beating (flat): a router spawn is refused unless its prompt is exactly a lifecycle phrase; each agent gets its own session, role, effort and writer records. Criterion 9 records whose hooks governed each worker. If that was the parent session's, a worker's role-specific refusals may not apply (finding). Seeking the wrong goal (worsening): the order works against the worsening machinery trend by removing per-phase sessions and, through the preflight discipline, repeated full gates. Shifting the burden (flat): directly removes recurring operator handoffs. Drift to low performance (flat but tight): executor cold start is 28,112 bytes against a 29,246 ceiling (1,134 bytes of headroom), and reviewer 27,037 against 28,884. Step 9 adds text to three roots and binds no byte figure (finding). Policy resistance (flat): one more refusal class (non-phrase spawns); per-worker caps keep the root-wide refusal. Tragedy of the commons: tokens move from one main thread into several workers. The cost line counts as removed 'the phase work itself' 'on a host that meters only the main thread', which is a metering shift, not a reduction (finding). Escalation: one new role and phrase and one generator for agent definitions; the four existing phrases stay. Success to the successful: reuses WO-187's generator and check rule instead of adding a second one.
orders.removalBalance: Yes in operator attention. One phrase per drive and one after the merge replace at least four sessions and their hand-carried handoffs per order, and full-gate repeats without a relevant change are removed. Added: a router role and root, per-agent identity in the harness host, per-worker sub-agent counting, a spawn refusal, a worktree-root grant, a `route` status reading, and role text in three roots. Tokens, wall-clock and context bytes are unknown until run. The metering line is not a cost removal.
orders.failureBehavior: Degrades. The four existing phrases stay, so if the router fails or refuses, the operator's per-phase sessions work as today. A refused spawn is typed, and the router records no lifecycle transition of its own. The root-wide sub-agent total is still reported and refused at the ceiling; an unattributable spawn is still counted as a stated minimum; an absent `router` budget entry reads as null.

findings.reason: Step 9 adds the preflight discipline to the executor root and the target-order branch to the executor, verifier and reviewer roots. Criteria 11 and 12 record cold-start bytes before and after but bind none. The cost table's acceptances show eleven cold-start ceiling raises since 2026-09-17 under the standing one-step route.
